evidence: The surviving solution defines `class DLX` and uses a `DLX` exact-cover search; the statement says `select exactly k` points and that `no two share the same X-coordinate, no two share the same Y-coordinate, and no two share the same Z-coordinate`.
affordance_in_statement: The grid spans from 1 to k along the X, Y, and Z axes; select exactly k anchor points; no two share the same X-coordinate, no two share the same Y-coordinate, and no two share the same Z-coordinate.
removal_suggestion: No semantics-preserving wording change can remove this affordance: with k possible values on each axis and exactly k selected points, the constraints are inherently a 3-dimensional matching/exact-cover instance. At most, avoid explicitly restating the condition as three separate uniqueness constraints and present it only through the pairwise distance formula.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Models the task as exact cover over the 3k coordinate-value columns and solves it with DLX.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Select exactly k points from coordinates ranging from 1 to k, with no repeated coordinate on any axis.

common_affordance: The intrinsic 3-dimensional exact-cover structure induced by selecting exactly k points from k-valued X, Y, and Z coordinates while requiring uniqueness on every axis.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Uses exponential backtracking over the available points and times out on adversarial instances.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit is available without changing the computational task.
